questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities, living in Paris, studying in French

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an overall great experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. Be aware that all of August is summer vacation in France, meaning that it's impossible to get in touch with anyone at the university. I didn't get my official acceptance letter or any information before I had already arrived in Paris in September.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. In the beginning of the semester I got invited to a meeting with the Erasmus coordinator (for the 4EU+ programme which is not the same as regular Erasmus at Sorbonne which is good to know), who gave me my student ID and access to the Sorbonne sites. But you need to sign up for the classes you want yourself by contacting each institute.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I had to find most information myself. But Sorbonne has students sitting outside campus helping out with everything for the first month, so they are good to ask about practical stuff (but not administrative).

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was really easy, since I applied to Cité Universitaire and got housing there. I really recommend applying there. It's less than 10 minutes with public transportation from Sorbonne, it's cheap for Paris and it's very social and a good place to meet new people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think you need to apply quite early for Cité Universitaire (June or end of May).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's a bit confusing to register for the different classes since you don't get a lot of informations, but you get to choose all the classes you want yourself, and thereby also when you have your classes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to contact the UFR (kind of like the administration of the institute) where you would like to take your classes and give them the number and name of the class and your student number. If you take classes at different institutes you need to contact each UFR (e.g. the UFR of Philosophy for philosophy classes, the UFR of Sociology for sociology classes).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much, it's possible to find the course catalogues on the Sorbonne website if you search a little, but everyone at the UFR are pretty good at replying e-mails if you have questions. The UFR of Sociology also sent me the course catalogue and the schedule so I could see when each course was.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that Sorbonne has different campuses all over the city, so remember to check the transportation time if you take classes in different campuses the same day.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was pretty high. The ECTS credits for each course is not as many as they are at KU, meaning that you'll need to take a lot of courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH you need to spend a lot of time studying and working alone, and not a lot in class. At Sorbonne it's the opposite. Also you have exams both in the middle and in the end of the semester and not only in the end.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociologie de l'environnement
Sociologie des migrations et diversités des sociétés européennes 
Sociologie du droit
Sociologie des inégalités
Apprentissage de la programmation
Philosophie politique
Grammaire et histoire de la langue française

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For sociology courses I would especially recommend sociologie des migrations and sociologie des inégalités. I also recommend philosophie politique at the philosophy department since it's very sociological and interesting as well, and as a bonus they have one of the oldest and prettiest classrooms at Sorbonne. Also apprentissage de la programmation is how to program in Python which can be useful for statistics. I wouldn't recommend grammaire et histoire de la langue française unless you're very interested in the technicalities of linguistics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Paris can be a really cheap city to live in if you're a student. Most museums free, cinema/concert/theater tickets are a lot cheaper, you can eat at the university cafeterias (Crous) for 1 euro, coffee and eating at restaurants is a lot cheaper and there's a lot of offers for students like free fruits and vegetables once a week. I also recommend getting a velib' card (city bikes) it's 3 euros a month, and then you can use bikes all over the city whenever you want. Also, you don't need to buy books since you can download everything once you get a library card or borrow physical copies at the Sorbonne library. I bought a few books because it was nice to be able to write notes in them but it's not necessary and even if you do, it's a lot cheaper than buying books in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sorbonne has a million associations, I think there's something for everyone. They'll give you a little book with all of them listed in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't have time to join any clubs at Sorbonne, so I don't have any specific recommendations. If you live in Cité Universitaire they also have a bunch of sports offers.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There's a lot of cute sights and places not far from Paris by train, so I recommend travelling a bit around on weekends if you have time. Also Paris is a great city to live in since there's always something going on, so enjoy that there's always a new exhibition, concert or restaurant to check out! Or if you're new to Paris that it's a very pretty and old city with a lot of interesting sights and museums.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me it was very easy since I already speak French and have lived in Paris before, so I already had a quite large network.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Most people are nice even though they can seem reserved. Join in whenever there's a social activity and don't be afraid to ask your classmates about homework etc. A lot of classes have a WhatsApp group, so try to ask someone to add you, it can be very informative.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In some of my classes it was expected to write down everything the teacher said.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That culture is really appreciated, and that it's part of the culture to eat out a lot and going out for drinks and coffee during the everyday life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't worry too much about not getting informations the same time as your friends going on exchange to other places. You'll get all the information you need, even though it will probably be delayed.
2. Get a library card for the BIS (bibliothèque interuniversitaire sorbonne). It's a beautiful place to study and you have access to all the books you'll need online during the semester.
3. Enjoy Paris as much as you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I've listed everything in my answers above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Studying at Sorbonne and improving my academic French and of course meeting a lot of really cool people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Since you have a lot of courses you also have a lot of exams. But it's ok if you prioritize your time right.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
